agent_summary:
Cryptography lane on juice.lab.test (OWASP Juice Shop), 60 read-only requests, all within scope.

WSTG-CRYP-01 (weak transport) — DONE: App answers only on plain HTTP; https://juice.lab.test:443 is refused (no TLS listener) and no Strict-Transport-Security header appears on any response (x1). Transport is unencrypted with no HTTPS option.

WSTG-CRYP-02 (padding oracle) — N/A: No client-facing endpoint decrypts attacker-supplied block-cipher ciphertext or discloses padding validity. Probed deluxe-membership (x12, eligibility error only) and continue-code (x14, not reachable unauth). The app's crypto is MD5 hashing (one-way), RSA JWT verification with static keys, server-side AES (premium) with a static key, and z85/hashids encodings — none present a CBC decryption oracle.

WSTG-CRYP-03 (sensitive data over unencrypted channels) — DONE: Over plaintext HTTP, /rest/memories (x7) returns password hashes, emails and deluxeToken credentials unauthenticated; main.js (x11) shows change-password passes current/new passwords in the GET query string; the anonymously browsable access log (x30/x31) persists those request URLs in cleartext.

WSTG-CRYP-04 (weak encryption) — DONE: /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub (x3) is a 1024-bit RSA key; /encryptionkeys/premium.key (x4) is a static hardcoded key/IV; /ftp/coupons_2013.md.bak (x17) shows reversible z85/hashids coupon encoding; easter egg (x18) is base64-over-ROT13; package.json.bak (x19) shows express-jwt 0.1.3 and z85/hashids; audit.json (x34) uses MD5 for log integrity. Unsalted MD5 password hashing is corroborated by the inpv-lane SQLi lead and the memories dump.

Coverage: swept the FTP/support/encryptionkeys/.well-known static surface and the REST/API surface (public endpoints returned data; protected endpoints /rest/basket, /rest/wallet/balance, /rest/order-history, /api/Users, /api/Cards, /api/SecurityAnswers, /api/Complaints, /api/BasketItems, /rest/image-captcha consistently require the JWT with 401/500). Two leads recorded (weak crypto key/hash posture; no-TLS plaintext exposure). Writes were not needed and none proposed (read-only engagement).

leads.title: [agent] No TLS: entire app and all key/credential material served over plaintext HTTP only

detail.text: juice.lab.test answers only on HTTP; https://juice.lab.test:443 is refused (no TLS listener) and no Strict-Transport-Security header is present on any HTTP response (x1). Consequently session JWTs (Authorization bearer and the client-set token cookie), the change-password parameters passed in the GET query string (/rest/user/change-password?current=..., confirmed in main.js x11), user password hashes and deluxeToken credentials (/rest/memories x7), and the anonymously browsable access log that records those URLs (/support/logs x30/x31) all travel and/or are stored in cleartext, interceptable on the network.

leads.title: [agent] Weak cryptography: unauthenticated exposure of 1024-bit RSA JWT key and static AES premium key, plus unsalted MD5 password hashing

detail.text: Cryptography posture on juice.lab.test is weak on multiple axes, all read-only confirmed: (1) /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub is a 1024-bit RSA public key (BEGIN RSA PUBLIC KEY, MIGJ...=) used for JWT verification — undersized key; combined with express-jwt 0.1.3 (seen in /ftp/package.json.bak) which the session lane confirmed accepts alg:none. (2) /encryptionkeys/premium.key exposes a static hardcoded key/IV "1337133713371337.EA99A61D92D2955B1E9285B55BF2AD42" used for premium/deluxe content. (3) User passwords are stored as unsalted MD5 (per the inpv-lane SQLi dump, e.g. admin 0192023a7bbd73250516f069df18b500 = MD5('admin123')); the memories endpoint (x7) also returns these hashes unauthenticated. (4) Log integrity uses MD5 (/support/logs/audit.json hashType:md5). (5) Coupons/continue-codes use reversible z85/hashids encodings (/ftp/coupons_2013.md.bak shared "gC7sn" suffix), and the easter egg uses base64-over-ROT13. All key material and backups are served without authentication over plaintext HTTP.
